title: Proper derived direct image comparison between small and big etale sites
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the size convention [def-weil-size-convention] and the big etale sites $B_X,B_Y$ and geometric morphisms $\pi_X,\pi_Y$ of [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. Let $f_s$ be the induced morphism of small etale topoi, and $f_b:\mathrm{Sh}(B_X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_Y)$ the relocalization morphism whose inverse image is $(f_b^{-1}H)(T\to X)=H(T\to X\to Y)$. Use ordinary right derived direct images of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and bounded-below subcategories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. For every $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{Et}})$ with torsion cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the canonical comparison is an isomorphism
$$\pi_Y^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{b,*}\pi_X^{-1}K\quad\text{in }D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(B_Y)).$$
The comparison is the base-change transformation for the commutative square $\pi_Y\circ f_b\cong f_s\circ\pi_X$, formed from its inverse/direct-image adjunctions. There is no common annihilator or invertibility assumption on the torsion orders.

source.place: Tag 0DDJ, lemma-compare-higher-direct-image-proper, part (2), including the canonical map specified in its proof.

proof.text: Form the canonical comparison $\beta_K:\pi_Y^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\to Rf_{b,*}\pi_X^{-1}K$ by [def-trf-topos-derived-base-change-map], taking the four coefficient rings to be constant $\mathbf Z$. Thus the four categories are derived categories of abelian sheaves, and the inverse-image functors are exact. The inverse-image square is the canonical big/small square of [lem-trf-big-small-etale-pullback-formula], rather than a freely chosen identification. The transpose of $\beta_K$ is $f_b^{-1}\pi_Y^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\cong\pi_X^{-1}f_s^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\to\pi_X^{-1}K$, with the last arrow induced by the small-site counit.

Fix any object $g:T\to Y$ of $B_Y$, and write $X_T=X\times_YT$, $h:X_T\to X$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$. By [lem-trf-big-small-etale-localization-derived-pushforward], $i_g$ is induced by the continuous and cocontinuous functor $u_g:T_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_Y$, and its inverse image is small-site restriction. For a big-site complex $N$ and any etale $U\to T$, [lem-trf-site-object-derived-sections-pullback] gives $R\Gamma(U,i_g^{-1}N)\cong R\Gamma(u_g(U),N)$; this specifies the actual small-site sections used here. The same localization node supplies
$$i_g^{-1}\pi_Y^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\cong g_s^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K,$$
$$i_g^{-1}Rf_{b,*}\pi_X^{-1}K\cong R(f_T)_{s,*}(i_h^{-1}\pi_X^{-1}K)\cong R(f_T)_{s,*}h_s^{-1}K.$$
Every $Rf_{s,*}$ in these expressions is applied to $K$ on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$; only $R(f_T)_{s,*}$ is applied to a complex on $(X_T)_{\mathrm{Et}}$.

The arrow-compatibility clause of [lem-trf-big-small-etale-localization-derived-pushforward] identifies $i_g^{-1}\beta_K$, under the comparisons in step 2, with the small-site exchange $g_s^{-1}Rf_{s,*}K\to R(f_T)_{s,*}h_s^{-1}K$. This is the precise exchange of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]: its transpose is the inverse-image square followed by $h_s^{-1}$ of the counit for $f_s$. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] to the cartesian square $(f,f_T,g,h)$ and the original $K$. Its hypotheses are exactly the properness of $f$, bounded-below $K$, and torsion of every cohomology sheaf of $K$, all assumed in the item. Therefore $i_g^{-1}\beta_K$ is an isomorphism for every $g$.

The family of all $i_g^{-1}$ is jointly conservative on $D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(B_Y))$ by [lem-trf-big-small-etale-localization-derived-pushforward]. Since every $i_g^{-1}\beta_K$ is an isomorphism by step 3, $\beta_K$ is an isomorphism. It is the canonical mate constructed in step 1, so this proves exactly the stated comparison. The small-site theorem was used with torsion cohomology alone; no common annihilator or invertibility hypothesis was introduced.
